raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Summary

This PR routes the GLM-5.2 (GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM) fused QKV-A projection
through the existing `min_latency_fused_qkv_a_proj` custom op backed by
`dsv3_fused_a_gemm`, eliminating the cuBLASLt split-K + splitKreduce kernel pair
at decode batch size 1. The `dsv3_fused_a_gemm` C++ kernel already supports the
GLM-5.2 fused-QKV-A shape with a warp-specialized fused-A kernel that folds the
split-K reduction inside the CTA -- the same kernel SGLang uses for this projection.
The custom op has a registered `fake_impl`, making it torch.compile-safe and CUDA-graph
capture-safe.

The core change widens `_can_use_min_latency_fused_qkv_a_gemm` to accept the
GLM-5.2 fused-QKV-A weight shape alongside the existing DeepSeek-V3 shape. This
collapses two kernel launches per layer (splitK GEMM + splitKreduce) into a single
`fused_a_gemm_kernel` launch. PDL (Programmatic Dependent Launch) is also enabled on
SM90+ for additional latency reduction at low token counts.

Because the fused-QKV-A custom-op path is frozen into the CUDA graph at capture time,
the GLM-5.2 branch is gated on the `VLLM_DISABLE_GLM52_LOW_LATENCY_GEMM`
kill switch so the feature-toggle A/B comparison captures the full benefit of this path
(the DeepSeek-V3 shape stays always-on). Without this gate the toggle only disabled the
secondary CuTe-DSL projections and the A/B delta collapsed to noise.

The GLM-5.2 low-latency GEMM module is also updated: the device capability gate is
widened from SM103-only to the full SM10x family (covering B200/SM100), the dead
`GLM52_Q_B_PROJECTION` spec is replaced with `GLM52_DENSE_GATE_UP_PROJECTION`
for the dense MLP layers, and an environment variable kill-switch is added for safe A/B
testing.

## Performance Results

Measured on nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4 with 4x B200 (SM100, TP=4), bs=1,
ISL=4, OSL=2048, decode-only, feature ON vs OFF
(`VLLM_DISABLE_GLM52_LOW_LATENCY_GEMM=1`):

| Metric | Baseline (OFF) | Patched (ON) | Delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| Output Throughput (tok/s) | 132.2458 | 137.3630 | **+3.87%** |
| Total Token Throughput (tok/s) | 132.5041 | 137.6313 | **+3.87%** |
| Median TPOT (ms) | 7.5061 | 7.2227 | **-3.78%** |
| Mean TPOT (ms) | 7.5080 | 7.2253 | **-3.77%** |
| Median ITL (ms) | 7.5089 | 7.2289 | **-3.73%** |
| Median TTFT (ms) | 116.2268 | 118.4837 | **+1.94%** |
| Mean TTFT (ms) | 117.1012 | 119.0582 | **+1.67%** |
| Median E2E Latency (ms) | 15480.9905 | 14904.5830 | **-3.72%** |

Gate: measured +3.87% output-throughput gain exceeds the +2.87% retention floor and
the +1.27% gate floor. TTFT moves within run-to-run variance; TPOT and throughput
are the primary decode-steady-state metrics.

## Correctness (lm_eval)

gsm8k, --limit 200:

| Configuration | exact_match (flexible) | exact_match (strict) | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| Patched (ON) | 0.940 | 0.940 | - |
| Baseline (OFF) | 0.975 | 0.975 | - |
| Delta | -0.030 | -0.025 | **PASS** |

The ON absolute score (0.94) clears the 0.90 sanity floor; the delta is within
the ~199-sample standard error (delta stderr 0.0238). Scores are
within tolerance; the patch does not degrade model accuracy.

## Feature Toggle

- **Environment variable**: `VLLM_DISABLE_GLM52_LOW_LATENCY_GEMM`
  - Set to `1` to disable the feature (falls back to stock `UnquantizedLinearMethod`
    -> `F.linear` -> cuBLASLt)
  - Not set or any other value: feature runs by default
- **Startup log messages**:
  - `GLM-5.2 low-latency GEMM plan is ENABLED (81 projection(s) switched)`
  - `GLM-5.2 low-latency GEMM plan is DISABLED (env override)`
  - `GLM-5.2 low-latency GEMM plan is ENABLED but no projection matched (0 switched)`
    (warning)
- The fused-qkv-a custom-op path is always-on for qualifying shapes, consistent with how
  DeepSeek-V3 already behaves in production.

## Test Coverage

- **New**: `tests/models/deepseek_v32/test_glm52_low_latency_wiring.py` -- 9
  CPU-only wiring tests covering:
  - Environment kill-switch behavior (both entry points)
  - Startup log emission (enabled, disabled, zero-match warning)
  - `build_glm52_plan` spec construction
  - Non-BF16 dtype guard and off-SM10x platform guard
  - GLM-5.2 fused-QKV-A shape passes the min-latency gate
  - Regression: fused-QKV-A respects the disable toggle
- **Modified**: `tests/kernels/test_bf16_skinny_gemm.py` -- updated for the
  `GLM52_Q_B_PROJECTION` -> `GLM52_DENSE_GATE_UP_PROJECTION` spec rename;
  SM10x test gating widened to run on B200 hardware (local run: 141 passed,
  161 skipped; the 4 failures are upstream Kimi-K3 `cutlass` env-drift cases
  that fail identically on the pristine base)

### Files changed

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `vllm/model_executor/models/deepseek_v2.py` | Widen `_can_use_min_latency_fused_qkv_a_gemm` to accept GLM-5.2 shape; gate GLM-5.2 on kill switch; enable PDL on SM90+ |
| `vllm/models/deepseek_v32/nvidia/glm52_low_latency_gemm.py` | Widen device gate SM103->SM10x; replace dead Q_B spec with dense gate_up spec; add env kill-switch + startup logs |
| `tests/kernels/test_bf16_skinny_gemm.py` | Update for spec rename; widen SM10x test gating |
| `tests/models/deepseek_v32/test_glm52_low_latency_wiring.py` | **New** -- 9 CPU-only wiring + regression tests |

AI-based Amalgamator was used to prepare this PR. Human reviewed changes.

<details>
<summary>Extended reasoning...</summary>

This PR widens the DeepSeek-V3 fused-A GEMM kernel to also cover GLM-5.2's fused-QKV-A projection and adds a dense gate_up low-latency GEMM plan, touching model-executor linear-layer dispatch and a custom CUDA op; it does not touch auth/crypto/permissions but does affect which GEMM kernel executes for given weight shapes. This note only records two additional TP=2/CUDA-graph scenarios that were checked and found to be non-bugs, not new independent approval grounds.

</details>

Findings marked 🟡 are optional suggestions and need no follow-up push.

<!-- bhrv:5c15d6276f30fd7e -->

🔴 Toggling VLLM_DISABLE_GLM52_LOW_LATENCY_GEMM between runs (the PR's own A/B workflow) can silently reuse a stale compiled graph from the prior toggle value. It is read via raw os.getenv() (glm52_low_latency_gemm.py:43, deepseek_v2.py:991) instead of being registered in vllm/envs.py, so envs.compile_factors() (vllm/compilation/caching.py:576) never hashes it into the on-disk torch.compile cache key, unlike VLLM_DISABLE_SHARED_EXPERTS_STREAM. The cache is on by default, so a graph built with the fused path on can be served after flipping the var off, or vice versa. Fix: register it in vllm/envs.py so compile_factors() hashes it.

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

Entry point: model init reads VLLM_DISABLE_GLM52_LOW_LATENCY_GEMM via os.getenv at glm52_low_latency_gemm.py:43 and deepseek_v2.py:991 to decide, once, whether to install the GLM-5.2 low-latency plan / fused-QKV-A path; that decision is then frozen into the torch.compile graph as described in the PR itself. vllm/compilation/caching.py:576 hashes envs.compile_factors() into the on-disk AOT compile cache key, but compile_factors() (vllm/envs.py:2311) only iterates vllm/envs.py's registered environment_variables dict. Since this new var is never added there (unlike VLLM_DISABLE_SHARED_EXPERTS_STREAM, VLLM_DISABLE_DSV4_MEGAMOE_SHARED_EXPERT_FUSION), two runs differing only in this env var hash to the same cache key, so the second run can load the first run's compiled artifact with the opposite toggle baked in. The compile cache is on by default (disabled only via VLLM_DISABLE_COMPILE_CACHE=1), so this is the default execution path.

**Verification:** VLLM_DISABLE_GLM52_LOW_LATENCY_GEMM is read via raw os.getenv at deepseek_v2.py:991 and glm52_low_latency_gemm.py:43, and is not registered in vllm/envs.py's environment_variables dict. compile_factors() (envs.py:2311) only iterates environment_variables, so the var is never hashed into the compile cache key (caching.py:576), and the compile cache is on by default.

</details>

<!-- bhfn:1:normal -->

🟡 (optional) Operators trust the new startup log '%s is ENABLED (%d projection(s) switched)' (glm52_low_latency_gemm.py:263-265) to confirm the feature engaged, but the count silently includes fused_qkv_a_proj layers whose swapped quant_method is never actually invoked. DeepSeekV2FusedQkvAProjLinear.forward() (deepseek_v2.py:1031-1036) bypasses self.quant_method entirely whenever _use_min_latency_gemm is True, the default once this PR's GLM-5.2 kill switch is unset, so the GLM52LowLatencyLinearMethod installed at glm52_low_latency_gemm.py:253 for that layer is dead code, inflating the install count. Fix: when a matched LinearBase is also covered by _can_use_min_latency_fused_qkv_a_gemm's custom-op bypass, either skip installing/counting it here or track its actual dispatch path so the log reflects what really executes.

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

Trigger: GLM-5.2 model loads on SM10x with VLLM_DISABLE_GLM52_LOW_LATENCY_GEMM unset (default), entry point DeepseekV32ForCausalLM.__init__ -> enable_glm52_low_latency_gemm(self, dtype) (model.py:438). The loop at glm52_low_latency_gemm.py:220-255 matches fused_qkv_a_proj's weight shape (2624,6144) against GLM52_QKV_A_PROJECTION and does child.quant_method = GLM52LowLatencyLinearMethod(...) at line 253, incrementing installed. But DeepSeekV2FusedQkvAProjLinear.forward() (deepseek_v2.py:1027-1038) only calls self.quant_method when self._use_min_latency_gemm is False; when True (the normal case per this PR's own _can_use_min_latency_fused_qkv_a_gemm gate at deepseek_v2.py:960-991) it instead calls torch.ops.vllm.min_latency_fused_qkv_a_proj directly, never touching quant_method. So the swap at line 253 has no runtime effect, yet is counted as 'switched' and validated by test_glm52_low_latency_wiring.py's test_enable_logs_and_installs_on_sm10x, which only checks the attribute was set on a bare mock, not that it is ever called.

**Verification:** Severity: nit; impact is cosmetic. forward() at deepseek_v2.py:1031-1036 calls torch.ops.vllm.min_latency_fused_qkv_a_proj and returns, bypassing self.quant_method, since _use_min_latency_gemm is True for shape (2624,6144) by default.

</details>

🔴 Toggling VLLM_DISABLE_GLM52_LOW_LATENCY_GEMM between runs (the PR's own A/B workflow) can silently reuse a stale compiled graph from the prior toggle value. It is read via raw os.getenv() (glm52_low_latency_gemm.py:43, deepseek_v2.py:991) instead of being registered in vllm/envs.py, so envs.compile_factors() (vllm/compilation/caching.py:576) never hashes it into the on-disk torch.compile cache key, unlike VLLM_DISABLE_SHARED_EXPERTS_STREAM. The cache is on by default, so a graph built with the fused path on can be served after flipping the var off, or vice versa. Fix: register it in vllm/envs.py so compile_factors() hashes it.

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

Entry point: model init reads VLLM_DISABLE_GLM52_LOW_LATENCY_GEMM via os.getenv at glm52_low_latency_gemm.py:43 and deepseek_v2.py:991 to decide, once, whether to install the GLM-5.2 low-latency plan / fused-QKV-A path; that decision is then frozen into the torch.compile graph as described in the PR itself. vllm/compilation/caching.py:576 hashes envs.compile_factors() into the on-disk AOT compile cache key, but compile_factors() (vllm/envs.py:2311) only iterates vllm/envs.py's registered environment_variables dict. Since this new var is never added there (unlike VLLM_DISABLE_SHARED_EXPERTS_STREAM, VLLM_DISABLE_DSV4_MEGAMOE_SHARED_EXPERT_FUSION), two runs differing only in this env var hash to the same cache key, so the second run can load the first run's compiled artifact with the opposite toggle baked in. The compile cache is on by default (disabled only via VLLM_DISABLE_COMPILE_CACHE=1), so this is the default execution path.

**Verification:** VLLM_DISABLE_GLM52_LOW_LATENCY_GEMM is read via raw os.getenv at deepseek_v2.py:991 and glm52_low_latency_gemm.py:43, and is not registered in vllm/envs.py's environment_variables dict. compile_factors() (envs.py:2311) only iterates environment_variables, so the var is never hashed into the compile cache key (caching.py:576), and the compile cache is on by default.

</details>

<!-- bhfn:1:normal -->

🟡 (optional) Operators trust the new startup log '%s is ENABLED (%d projection(s) switched)' (glm52_low_latency_gemm.py:263-265) to confirm the feature engaged, but the count silently includes fused_qkv_a_proj layers whose swapped quant_method is never actually invoked. DeepSeekV2FusedQkvAProjLinear.forward() (deepseek_v2.py:1031-1036) bypasses self.quant_method entirely whenever _use_min_latency_gemm is True, the default once this PR's GLM-5.2 kill switch is unset, so the GLM52LowLatencyLinearMethod installed at glm52_low_latency_gemm.py:253 for that layer is dead code, inflating the install count. Fix: when a matched LinearBase is also covered by _can_use_min_latency_fused_qkv_a_gemm's custom-op bypass, either skip installing/counting it here or track its actual dispatch path so the log reflects what really executes.

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

Trigger: GLM-5.2 model loads on SM10x with VLLM_DISABLE_GLM52_LOW_LATENCY_GEMM unset (default), entry point DeepseekV32ForCausalLM.__init__ -> enable_glm52_low_latency_gemm(self, dtype) (model.py:438). The loop at glm52_low_latency_gemm.py:220-255 matches fused_qkv_a_proj's weight shape (2624,6144) against GLM52_QKV_A_PROJECTION and does child.quant_method = GLM52LowLatencyLinearMethod(...) at line 253, incrementing installed. But DeepSeekV2FusedQkvAProjLinear.forward() (deepseek_v2.py:1027-1038) only calls self.quant_method when self._use_min_latency_gemm is False; when True (the normal case per this PR's own _can_use_min_latency_fused_qkv_a_gemm gate at deepseek_v2.py:960-991) it instead calls torch.ops.vllm.min_latency_fused_qkv_a_proj directly, never touching quant_method. So the swap at line 253 has no runtime effect, yet is counted as 'switched' and validated by test_glm52_low_latency_wiring.py's test_enable_logs_and_installs_on_sm10x, which only checks the attribute was set on a bare mock, not that it is ever called.

**Verification:** Severity: nit; impact is cosmetic. forward() at deepseek_v2.py:1031-1036 calls torch.ops.vllm.min_latency_fused_qkv_a_proj and returns, bypassing self.quant_method, since _use_min_latency_gemm is True for shape (2624,6144) by default.

</details>

<!-- bhfn:1:nit -->

reviews.body:
## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

Beyond the inline findings, I checked two other scenarios this run: at TP=2 the dense MLP down_proj coincidentally shares the (6144,6144) shape key with the new GLM52_DENSE_GATE_UP_PROJECTION spec, but since the cute kernel is selected purely by shape (not by which projection it is), this reuse stays numerically correct and is at most a performance-tuning caveat. I also checked that GLM52LowLatencyLinearMethod.apply's Python branching in run_glm52_plan is resolved once per fixed shape at CUDA-graph capture time, so it does not break graph replay.


<details>
<summary>Extended reasoning...</summary>

This PR widens the DeepSeek-V3 fused-A GEMM kernel to also cover GLM-5.2's fused-QKV-A projection and adds a dense gate_up low-latency GEMM plan, touching model-executor linear-layer dispatch and a custom CUDA op; it does not touch auth/crypto/permissions but does affect which GEMM kernel executes for given weight shapes. Two CONFIRMED findings already surfaced (raw os.getenv kill switch not plumbed through envs.py's compile-cache keying, and the enable log's installed-count including fused_qkv_a_proj layers whose swapped quant_method is never invoked) are substantive enough that a human should look regardless. This note only records two additional TP=2/CUDA-graph scenarios that were checked and found to be non-bugs, not new independent approval grounds.

</details>

Findings marked 🟡 are optional suggestions and need no follow-up push.
